 "architecture": "Single-file rule bot with a fixed priority ladder for movement plus one utility-scored step for combat movement; aiming/fire and looting run as separate passes every tick. Module-level feature switches allow A/B runs. Movement ladder, in order: (1) outside the zone: path to the current zone centre, boost if energy above 20; (2) any known enemy mech (seen or within 5 s memory): combat movement, except a \"patient\" case (target unseen, it has not hit us in 5 s, our HP below 50%) which skips the chase; (3) supply drop if eligible; (4) zone safety: if within a margin (15% of the safe radius, clamped 8-30 m) of the safe circle's edge, walk to its centre, boosting only in the last 8 s before the shrink; when the safe radius is 30 m or less go to the final point; (5) walk to remembered loot (better weapon, cubes); (5b) walk to remembered drones/crates (farm); (6) shoot a visible drone or crate while holding a range of about 35 m (drone) or 25 m (crate) with slow strafing; (7) drift toward the next circle centre until within 45% of its radius, else stand. \"Safe circle\" means the next circle once the shrink is 25 s away, otherwise the current one. Target choice: lowest of distance + 80 x target HP fraction + 250 if not in line of fire, minus 30 stickiness for the current target; it does not distinguish hunters from idle house bots. Threat list: top three enemies by estimated DPS at their distance (gun 100, laser 131, lightning 240 inside 47 m, mortar 60 between 20 and 235 m), tripled if charging a laser with aim within 0.2 rad of us, discounted by distance. A free-for-all detector (two or more deaths not caused by us) only sets a label. Runtime hygiene: garbage collector frozen and run manually between ticks, optional work skipped past 20-22 ms, slow ticks logged.",
 "navigation": "Map model is a 2.5D raster on the 1 m terrain lattice: per cell the lowest base and highest top of covering buildings, with bridges in a separate layer so they can be walked and shot under. Line of sight is a 1 m step march along the segment (skipping the first 2 m and last 1.5 m), blocked by buildings, bridges and terrain; trees are ignored for shots. Walk grid at 2 m: a cell is blocked if any of its four lattice points has a solid between step height and head height or the ground varies more than 2.2 m inside it; a 6 m map border is blocked; blocked cells are dilated by one cell; connected regions are labelled. Path planning is weighted A* (heuristic weight 1.4, octile, no corner cutting, cap 90,000 nodes) sliced across ticks with an 8 ms budget; the goal snaps to the nearest free cell in the start's region. Follower: goes straight if the line is clear and under 60 m; replans when the goal moves more than 12 m, every 6 s, or 1.5 s after a failed plan; abandons the path when more than 15 m off it; steers at the farthest waypoint within 24 m reachable in a straight line. Paths are used only while on the ground, for every long walk (zone, loot, drops, hunting an unseen enemy). Local steering probes three parallel lines 3, 5.5 and 8 m ahead and tries angular offsets up to about 2.5 rad, preferred side first; jumps if nothing is clear. Stuck handling: if it commanded movement for 0.8 s and moved under 2 m, it flips the preferred side, picks a heading 1.2-1.6 rad off (fully random every third time), holds it 1.2 s while jumping and jetting when airborne with energy above 8, and discards the path. No roof or deliberate jet routes; loot more than 3.5 m above it is ignored.",
 "aiming_and_fire_control": "Gun: three fixed-point iterations of linear lead using the observed velocity (vertical velocity only when above 1 m/s; 3 m muzzle offset subtracted), aimed at body centre; fires only when the target is in line of fire, inside 95% of range, the magazine is ready, and the actual torso aim is within an angular tolerance equal to 0.75 of the target radius over distance plus 0.004 rad. Reload when empty; with no target, reload below 60% of the magazine. Laser: starts charging when in range and the target is visible or within 140 m even if hidden; holds the charge; within 0.2 s of full it switches from the lead aim to the direct line; releases at full charge when on target, or early if the partial-charge damage would finish the target, and at any charge on crates; keeps holding if the target disappears (so the 2 s auto-fire can waste the shot). Lightning: fires when the target is visible, inside 95% of range, energy above cost + 6 and yaw error under 80% of the cone figure; takes over the yaw when no gun solution or under 30 m. Mortar: only beyond 28 m and only when the target is hidden, there is no gun solution, or the gun is empty/reloading, and never while a laser charge is held; low arc when visible, high arc when hidden, two lead iterations with time of flight, fires within 0.02 rad. With no target the torso faces the last damage/sound bearing for 3 s, otherwise sweeps about 1.5 rad either side of the walking direction, or spins in place when standing. Useful rulebook detail confirmed while checking this: the lightning cone is \"within 30 degrees of aim yaw\" (a 30 degree half-angle), and it still fires and costs energy without a target.",
 "survival_and_anti_squad_tactics": "Combat movement scores 13 candidates (stand still plus 12 headings 30 degrees apart), each evaluated at the point reached after 0.7 s (half speed while charging a laser), skipping headings blocked within 3-6 m. Score terms: +1.5 for line of fire to the target from that point (+4 when its own laser is within 0.12 s of full, the \"peek\"); minus 0.8 x (summed DPS of threats that can see the point)/150; minus 8 per threat charging a laser at it that can see the point; range-band penalties (0.03 per metre too close, 0.02 per metre too far); a pull toward nearby loot; minus 0.25 per metre inside 58 m of any lightning holder; minus 25 plus 1 per metre for leaving the current zone and a small graded penalty outside 90% of the safe circle; minus 0.5 for standing still while exposed; +0.3 for moving roughly perpendicular to the target while exposed; +0.4 for keeping roughly the previous heading; small random jitter. Range bands: 75-165 m with a laser, 12-32 m with lightning, 40-105 m otherwise; lower bound raised to 60 m against a lightning holder. Boost when energy is above 30 and a laser is being charged at it or a lightning holder is within 62 m; 30% chance to jump when dodging a charge. Unseen target beyond 60% of the band's far edge: path to it, boosting if far. Retreat-and-regenerate (leave below 33% HP when the main threat is healthier or there are two threats, hide with cover weight 3.0, hold fire unless the target is under 25% HP so the 5 s regen timer can start, return above 75%) exists but is switched off at HEAD; so is hiding during its own laser charge. Net effect at HEAD: no regen cycles and no deliberate line-of-sight breaking except against a charging laser. Nothing targets the single early hunter specifically, and nothing changes after the point where all house bots hunt. A stealth mode (off at HEAD) was built as a probe: precomputed 4 m concealment map shipped as a 48 KB file (for each walkable spot, the fraction of 120 sample observers at 30/55/90/130/175 m in 24 directions that can see it, with tree canopy counted beyond 45 m), walk at 38% command so speed stays under the 5 m/s footstep-sound threshold, sit in the best hidden spot within 150 m, do not start fights, and switch to fighting for 6 s after any sign of being found (damage, enemy within 45 m, or an enemy within 200 m aiming within 0.35 rad of us).",
 "loot_weapons_upgrades": "Weapon preference laser > lightning > mortar; the gun is always kept (a laser + lightning, no-gun loadout exists behind a switch that is off). Takes anything into an empty slot, otherwise swaps out the weaker special when the new one ranks higher, never while a laser charge is held. Remembers pickups for 120 s and cubes for 45 s, forgetting them when it gets within 30 m with a clear view and they are gone. Loot walk value is gain x 40/(distance + 20) for weapons within 170 m and a fixed 1.2 weight for cubes within 110 m, only inside the safe circle, cubes only until 10 (stat cap). During fights, cubes within 45 m and upgrade weapons within 70 m add a linearly decaying bonus to combat-movement candidates so kill drops get collected. Farming (on at HEAD): remembers drones for 90 s and crates for 240 s, walks to them within 220 m when no mech is known, HP is above 45% and cubes are under 10, valuing drones about 1.5 times crates; shoots visible drones within 75 m (110 m with a laser) if HP is above 50% or the drone attacked it, and crates within 70 m (110 m with a laser). Upgrade order is defensive: plating, armor, nanites, laser damage, laser charge, gyros, lightning efficiency, gun damage, gun rate, then the rest; an offence-first order exists but is unused. Supply drops: considered within 320 m if the drop lands no later than 12 s after its walking arrival time, skipped if another mech already has over 2 s of capture progress or any top threat is within 70 m of it; stands still inside the ring. Drops rank below fighting any known mech.",
 "zone_and_endgame": "Outside the zone it paths to the current centre with boost. Treats the next circle as the required circle from 25 s before each shrink; moves in when within the edge margin and boosts only in the last 8 s. Combat movement gets a hard penalty for leaving the current zone and a graded one for leaving the safe circle (v2 change). When the required circle is 30 m or smaller it walks to the next circle's centre and stands on it, slowing as it approaches (v1 fix: earlier versions ran circles around the point). Otherwise idles by drifting to within 45% of the next radius of the next centre. No late-game plan for the phase when every house bot hunts.",
 "housebot_observations": "No direct observation of house-bot behaviour on the real scorer is recorded; everything is inferred from four real scores. Their first squad model: house bots share vision, never damage each other, hunters are assigned weakest tier first, one hunter at the start plus one more per two kills, everyone hunts after 300 s, non-hunters never engage or retaliate and just wander at 60% speed to random points within 60% of the safe radius (new point every 25 s), house aim noise at 3x their base profiles. Base scripted profiles (aim noise rad / reaction lag s / strafe fraction): easy 0.014/0.40/0.25, medium 0.010/0.30/0.45, hard 0.006/0.18/0.65, expert 0.004/0.10/0.85; they aim at our lagged position with linear gun lead and fire within 0.02 rad. Assumed house loadout: gun plus a second weapon (50% laser, 25% lightning, 25% mortar) with preferred fight ranges laser 130 m, gun 90 m, lightning 28 m, mortar 120 m. That model overpredicted their v2. Their second model, which they say reproduces \"the wall all versions hit\" near 4: easy bots stay weak and scripted, but medium, hard and expert hunters run the author's own v2 combat logic with only small added aim noise (0.006, 0.003, 0.0015 rad) and always know where the player is. Implication they drew: medium-and-up house bots fight about as well as a competent custom bot and effectively always know your position. My inference from their model: with weakest-first hunters and four easy bots, a score near 4 corresponds to killing the easy tier and then losing to the first medium-or-better hunters. They submitted a stealth variant explicitly to test \"do house bots need to see us?\"; no result is recorded, and the next commits went back to the farming variant, which suggests hiding did not pay (not documented).",

 "novel_ideas": [
  "Calibrating a stand-in squad against known real scores of several bot versions (including the starter at 1.15), and treating a mismatch on the next real score as evidence the squad model is wrong rather than the bot.",
  "Making the stand-in medium/hard/expert hunters run a competent bot's own combat logic with tier-dependent aim noise and perfect knowledge of the player's position, keeping only the easy tier as weak scripted bots; this was what reproduced a wall near 4.",
  "Hunter schedule as a formula: one hunter initially, one more per two kills, all after 300 s, assigned weakest tier first; non-hunters passive.",
  "Precomputed concealment map shipped with the bot (cheap lookup at run time) plus silent walking below the footstep-sound speed, used as a probe of whether the squad needs sight or sound to find the player.",
  "Loot as an additive pull inside the combat-movement score, so kill drops (cubes + 2 and the weapon) are collected without leaving the fight.",
  "Lightning kiting: a distance-proportional penalty inside 58 m of any lightning holder plus boosting away inside 62 m, since lightning is the highest close-range DPS and shorts lasers.",
  "Hard zone penalty inside the combat-movement scorer so dodging never walks out of the circle.",
  "Laser peek: weight line of fire much higher only in the last 0.12 s before full charge, and switch from lead aim to direct line for the release.",
  "Hold fire while retreating so the 5 s no-damage regen timer can start, unless the target is nearly dead.",
  "Module switches settable from the simulator command line for quick A/B runs, and a per-match trace that prints which tier and weapon dealt the damage.",
  "Seed-salt variants of an unchanged bot to sample scorer variance."
 ],
 "apparent_weaknesses": [
  "Best documented real score 4.04 is under the 4.23 qualification line; three rounds of added machinery produced no measurable real gain over v0.",
  "At HEAD there is no retreat, no regen cycle and effectively no cover use: the cover weight only applies while retreating (off), and a single gun threat's exposure penalty (about 0.5) is smaller than the line-of-fire bonus (1.5), so it stands and trades in the open except against a charging laser.",
  "Fights every known mech and never reasons about who the hunter is; by its own squad model each two kills add a hunter, and nothing prepares for the all-hunt phase or the stronger tiers.",
  "The squad simulator has many free parameters fitted to three or four numbers, and the strong hunters are the author's own bot, so results are partly circular; it mispredicted v2 by about 2.5 points before refitting.",
  "Decision-time risk: pure-Python line-of-sight marching for up to 13 candidates x 3 threats x 2 rays per tick on one CPU; when the 22 ms guard trips, later headings are never evaluated, biasing movement toward the first few compass directions.",
  "Line of sight uses a merged 2.5D raster (one base/top per cell, 1 m steps, ends skipped), so overhangs and stacked structures are wrong and thin geometry can be missed; trunks and canopy are not considered for being seen.",
  "Exposure is judged at one point 0.7 s ahead with no memory of cover beyond that; no path-level cover planning.",
  "Laser charge starts on hidden targets within 140 m and is held indefinitely, halving speed and risking the 2 s auto-fire into a wall.",
  "Gun lead is first-order on instantaneous velocity with no check that the lead point is unobstructed; no handling of strafing reversals.",
  "Leaving the zone sends it to the current centre rather than the nearest safe point; the endgame stands still on the final centre, which is predictable when 15 bots converge.",
  "No roof or jet navigation; elevated loot and crates are ignored."
